depth: The depth map presents a downward-looking egocentric scene in which the seated camera wearer looks at their towel-covered lap, about 0.4–0.6 m below, and a raised leg/footrest structure 0.3–0.5 m away supporting a round UV nail lamp. The left-side supply caddy is lower and approximately 0.6–0.8 m distant, while the floor appears darkest at 1.0–1.2 m below. Over the 5 frames, the camera wearer rotates slightly rightward. A second person sits in the upper-right area, 0.5–0.8 m away, facing the camera wearer’s lap with their head and upper torso outside the frame above; in frames 3–5, their right hand rests on the bright white nail lamp, 0.3–0.4 m from the camera. The camera wearer’s two hands rise from the lower-left and bottom edges at 0.5–0.7 m in frames 1–3, then move toward and touch the other person’s fingers at 0.3–0.4 m in frames 4–5. Every visible item—the left supply caddy, handheld lap control, lamp, and the other person’s extended hand—is reachable by both people and separated by under 0.5 m. Relative to RGB alone, the depth map clearly distinguishes the height levels of the elevated foreground hands and lamp, the mid-depth lap, and the lower recessed tray and floor, including the overlapping depth layers created when the camera wearer reaches over the lamp in frames 4 and 5. Nevertheless, bright white surfaces are represented unreliably in frames 1 and 2: the white lamp and padded leg rest become almost uniformly saturated at maximum brightness, so their relative distances cannot be distinguished.
segmentation: The segmentation map traces the scene footprints of both people: the camera wearer fills the lower-left and central lap region, 0.4–0.7 m away, while the second person occupies the upper-right, 0.5–0.8 m away, facing the centre with their head and torso cut off by the frame. It also marks the rounded nail lamp on the raised rest, 0.3–0.5 m away and reachable by each person. Across the 5 frames, the masks follow the camera wearer’s limbs as they first reach into the supply caddy on the left, 0.6–0.8 m away, in frames 1–2, then move upward and toward the centre in frames 4–5, overlapping the other person’s hand on top of the lamp at 0.3–0.4 m. Their hands increasingly obscure the lamp as they come together. The map helps define the lamp’s rounded outline in frames 1 and 3 and keeps the two people’s limb areas separate in frames 1, 4, and 5, but it does not segment smaller reachable objects, including the left-side supply caddy and the corded controller lying on the lap. Its class labels and mask consistency are also highly unreliable: the nail lamp is incorrectly identified as a 'banana' in frames 1 and 3, the chair edge at upper left is labelled a 'laptop' in frame 2, both people are combined into one 'person' mask in frames 2 and 3, and extensive unsegmented black holes remain over the towel-covered lap and background chair.
pose: On a black background, the pose map displays 2D skeletal keypoints that isolate hand and body arrangements within the 0.3–0.7 m working area in front of and below the downward-facing camera wearer, excluding all background items and the cropped upper torsos. In frames 1 and 3, one small magenta hand skeleton is visible at the lower left, about 0.6–0.7 m away, where the camera wearer’s left hand reaches into the supply tray. Frame 3 additionally shows a larger magenta hand skeleton at the top centre, 0.3–0.4 m away, representing the other person’s right hand lying flat with spread fingers directed downward toward the camera wearer. In frame 4, two magenta hand skeletons sit close together around the centre, less than 0.1 m apart and 0.3–0.4 m from the camera, as the camera wearer’s left hand comes from the lower left toward the other person’s downward-pointing hand. In frame 5, overlapping magenta and yellow skeletal lines appear at centre-right while the camera wearer’s two hands clasp and partly hide the other person’s fingers. In comparison with RGB, the pose map directly shows finger-joint articulation, orientation, and the closeness between hands throughout the interaction in frames 3–5, confirming that neither individual’s head nor gaze appears in view. However, its completeness and anatomical assignment are unreliable: it omits every hand in frame 2 and misses the camera wearer’s right hand in frames 1, 3, and 4, while frame 5 invents a deformed yellow torso-and-limb skeleton across the interacting hands and elevated leg rest.
